terms.definition: The offensive players tasked with tagging opponents. In an active turn, 8 chasers sit in the cross-lane squares while 1 active chaser pursues the defenders.
The defensive players on the field entering in batches of 3, striving to evade tags and maximize their survival time inside the court boundaries.
The mandatory vocal shout that must be uttered aloud simultaneously while tapping a seated teammate on their back to hand over the active chase.
The 24-meter long, 30cm wide line joining the two posts. Active chasers cannot cross this line directly; doing so incurs a foul.
The 8 perpendicular paths (16m long x 35cm wide) cutting across the central lane where sitting squares are established.
Two upright wooden poles (120-125cm high, 9-10cm diameter) standing at each end of the central lane, used by chasers to swing around and legally reverse direction.
The 1.5m x 16m territory behind each post where the direction rule is suspended, allowing the chaser to rotate or choose any course of sprint.
A fundamental rule stating an active chaser must maintain their chosen forward momentum and cannot turn backwards mid-lane without circling a post.
In Ultimate Kho Kho (UKK), a special designated attacker who holds the superpower to run in both directions freely across cross-lanes.
An acrobatic aerial leap by an active chaser to touch a running defender before landing on the mat, scoring 3 points in UKK.
Using one arm to grip the wooden post while horizontally hurling the body outward to tag an evasive defender near the pole line.
When a defender batch survives on court for over 2 minutes and 30 seconds against constant chases, earning bonus defense points.
